memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Three days later, while all of them were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords and attacked the unsuspecting city, killing every male. They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword and took Dinah from Shechem's house and left. The sons of Jacob came upon the dead bodies and looted the city where their sister had been defiled. They seized their flocks and herds and donkeys and everything else of theirs in the city and out in the fields. They carried off all their wealth and all their women and children, taking as plunder everything in the houses." - Gen 34:25-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What began as righteous anger now becomes something monstrous. While the men of the city lie helpless and in pain, Simeon and Levi take their swords and slaughter every male. Then all the brothers loot the city, seizing flocks, wealth, and even carrying off the women and children as plunder. A crime had been done against one woman — and in response, an entire city is destroyed and countless innocent people are harmed.

The Bible records this without approving it. In fact, years later, Jacob would speak a solemn word of judgment over Simeon and Levi for this very act: "Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel!" (Gen 49:7). God's own verdict, spoken through Jacob, condemns their violence.

Here is the sobering lesson: revenge, once unleashed, rarely stops where justice would. The brothers had a real grievance, but they returned evil for evil and then multiplied it far beyond all measure. Two wrongs never make a right; they only deepen the darkness. And notice the bitter irony — men who claimed to defend their sister's honour ended by treating other women and children as plunder.

This is why God says, "Do not take revenge... 'It is mine to avenge; I will repay,' says the Lord" (Rom 12:19). When we take vengeance into our own hands, we almost always go too far. Leave justice to the God who judges perfectly, and do not let a real wrong turn you into a doer of greater evil.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I tempted to take revenge into my own hands?
2. Do I see how vengeance rarely stops where justice would?
3. Can I entrust justice to God rather than repaying evil with evil?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am wronged, guard me from the trap of revenge. Help me not to return evil for evil, but to entrust all justice to You, who judge perfectly and repay in Your time. Amen.
